newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Four killed as Lesotho police clash with workers.
newsitem.headline: Four killed as Lesotho police clash with workers.

text.p: At least four people were killed in a clash at the weekend between police and dismissed Basotho workers from the major Lesotho Highlands water project, police said on Monday.
"Four people were killed and four others received injuries in clashes between the police and workers," police headquarters in Maseru said in a statement.

Police confirmed the incident, at a water project site at Butha Buthe about 110 km (69 miles) from Maseru, took place on Saturday during a police raid to enforce a High Court order for the sacked workers to vacate the site.
The workers refused to leave, and police opened fire, the statement said.
Maseru police only confirmed four people were wounded but witnesses at the scene told local reporters that at least 17 were hurt.

The workers were among 2,000 workers dismissed by two contractors involved in the highlands water project last Thursday for a week-long illegal strike which started on September 6, in protest against alleged racial discrimination.

The Lesotho Highlands Water Project is a $5 billion joint venture by Lesotho and South Africa which aims to harness the tiny landlocked country's abundant water resources for the benefit of both southern African countries.
